answer: Reputation-weighted task routing works as a prism that splits each identity’s history into a visible trust score. A new clone starts at zero and must complete a slow probationary bridge of low-value jobs before bidding on high-value work, while an established identity crosses that bridge instantly. Every clone therefore pays the full probation time plus lost bidding opportunities, a cost that compounds per identity and makes mass cloning more expensive than honest participation. The system also acts as a jetty, throttling how fast fresh identities can reach profitable tasks.
